problem: In VLN-CE, panoramic task-specific small models beat fine-tuned MLLMs in simulation but overfit to scene styles, are opaque, and transfer poorly. MLLM-based methods are weaker and lack robustness. Rule-based controllers (random rotation 'Tryout') and depth-dependent waypoint predictors are unsafe and impractical for real robots.
motivation: Small panoramic models and MLLMs have complementary strengths: the small model gives fast, reliable in-domain decisions, while the MLLM offers commonsense reasoning and interpretability. Combining them only where the small model is uncertain could give robust, generalizable navigation. Real deployment also needs sensor-realistic low-level modules, since consumer panoramic cameras lack aligned depth.
key_idea: Run a causal-learning dual-branch small panoramic planner (RSMP) and invoke a zero-shot panoramic-prompted CoT MLLM reasoner (RLMR) only when conformal prediction shows RSMP is uncertain, fusing the two by the size of the prediction set.
insight: Conformal-prediction-based fusion beats calling the MLLM alone, an extra VLM arbiter, entropy and MC-dropout uncertainty (Tab. UCM: CP SR 64.64-65.34 val-unseen vs 62.59 RLMR-only, 63.98 arbiter, 64.04 entropy, 61.67 MC dropout), and is stable across tau. The MLLM mostly helps in stricter success radii (SDT=1: +8.9% SR over RSMP, +75% over RLMR) and in the real world, where the 72B zero-shot model (55% SR) far exceeds a LoRA-tuned 7B (35%), which overfits. The dual-branch structure and SV-pretrained weights give most of the small-model gain (Tab. RSMP: 60.07 to 64.36 SR val-unseen from adding the local branch).
method: RSMP: DUET-style dual-graph (global topological + local) planner initialized from ScaleVLN weights, with CLIP-H/14 and depth ResNet-50, fusing local and global logits with a learnable weight w; outputs a softmax over waypoint candidates.

Causal learning: back-door adjustment (confounder dictionaries for observable room-type/keyword cues) and front-door adjustment (mediator via multi-head attention) modules from GOAT, inserted into language, vision and memory features.

RLMR (PVP + CoT): Qwen2.5-VL-72B (zero-shot, vLLM) receives the full equirectangular panorama with projected candidate waypoint markers and a semi-transparent mask on rear-view edges; a structured prompt (system, instruction, history, candidates, small-model suggestion) drives 5-step CoT ending in a decision with confidence.

UCM: split conformal prediction on RSMP (nonconformity 1-p, calibration on 50% of train, threshold tau); if the prediction set is a singleton, execute RSMP's action; otherwise query RLMR on the set and fuse p=(1-a)p_RSMP+a p_RLMR with a=min(|C|/10,0.9).
Simulation low-level control: replace the rule-based Tryout controller with a learned DDPPO RGB-D point-goal policy for obstacle avoidance and deadlock recovery.

Real-world waypoints: training-free LiDAR occupancy cost map, K-means (K=10) over navigable cells, filter close-to-obstacle/duplicate centers, TF transform to robot/world frames (0.03s vs 0.42s for the WP net on Jetson Orin Nano).
Real-world control: online SLAM with ROS move_base as local controller; the RSMP variant trained without depth is used, since the panoramic camera has no aligned depth.

setting.backbone: RSMP (~1B, DUET/ETPNav-style with CLIP-H/14, trained) + Qwen2.5-VL-72B (frozen, zero-shot) as RLMR; DDPPO point-goal policy
setting.training_data: RSMP fine-tuned on the standard R2R-CE train split only (init from ScaleVLN weights pretrained on MP3D+HM3D augmented data); REVERIE-CE fine-tuned from R2R-CE checkpoint; RLMR zero-shot (7B variant LoRA-tuned on the 72B model's correct train responses)
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (12 views) + depth in simulation; real world: Insta360 panoramic RGB + 3D LiDAR, no depth
setting.action_space: high-level: candidate waypoints on a topological graph; low-level: DDPPO point-goal policy (FORWARD/TURN/STOP) in sim, SLAM move_base in real
setting.privileged: none (simulated panoramic depth for the waypoint predictor in sim; no maps in the real world)

numbers.extra: trained on R2R train only; ranked 1st on the VLN-CE leaderboard

results: CLASH ranks 1st on the VLN-CE leaderboard with test-unseen SR 66 / SPL 58, a relative +13.79% SR and +13.73% SPL over g3D-LF (58 / 51). On REVERIE-CE val-unseen it reaches SR 35.4 / SPL 26.6 vs g3D-LF 34.4 / 23.8. It also transfers to a real wheeled robot without in-domain fine-tuning and clearly outperforms ETPNav there.
limitations: Large-model inference is expensive (72B ~6.9 s per call vs 0.225 s for RSMP), hindering real-time use; the 7B LoRA model is cheaper but drops to ~35% real-world SR.
At SDT=3 CLASH occasionally slightly trails RSMP alone, and causal learning gives small gains on R2R; failures come from ambiguous instructions and fine-grained grounding.
Real-world evaluation is small (40 episodes) and models are insensitive to directional cues, aligning mainly at the object level.
